header.act: ACT VII — TO THE POLISH BORDER
player.speaker: Front Commissar
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.reaction-briliant.text: The Kassa presses are sending Slovak appeals north. My organisers are already talking about a republic. I need to know which committees can actually meet before I let them put names on a proclamation.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.reaction-tactical.text: We've taken Kassa, but the road to Eperjes is still a problem. I can't send organisers up it on the strength of a leaflet. When can your columns go through?
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.reaction-victory.text: The appeals are going north from Kassa and committees are forming. Several want to speak for the new republic. I have to get them into the same room before one announces it alone.
line.callback-kassa.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.callback-kassa.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-kassa.text: Kassa is ours, and the junction with it. Every train the Czechoslovak command wanted to move south now goes the long way or not at all.
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.text: The Kassa pursuit got ahead of the repaired supply line. I have commanders asking to go farther and trains that can't reach them. Set the limit before I issue another movement order.
line.callback-doctrine-methodical.text: We waited for Stromfeld's guns and railway crews at Kassa. He has supplied divisions now. I still think we gave the enemy useful hours; we'll see what they've done with them at the next position.
line.presov-printing-room.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.presov-printing-room.text: Before we print another appeal, read this question from Eperjes: will their councils govern, or will Budapest? I need an answer I can give the organisers. They're watching what our battalions do.
line.stromfeld-opening.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.stromfeld-opening.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.stromfeld-opening.text: Bártfa would cut across the separating enemy fronts, near the Polish border. Supply gets difficult that far north. I need the ammunition route agreed, and someone speaking to the villages along it.
line.janousek-message.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.janousek-message.text: Workers in the occupied towns ask whether the Red Army has come to restore old Hungarian rule or to help them elect councils of their own. Forbid undisciplined requisition, publish orders in the local languages, and make the answer visible before nationalist officers provide one of their own.
line.landler-national-answer.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-national-answer.text: Some of these soldiers want Kassa back in Hungary. They haven't marched north to create a separate state. Tell them what you're proposing before you ask them to defend it.
line.janousek-internationalist-reply.tex: Then help me tell them. We can't ask Slovak workers to reject Prague and accept orders from Budapest instead. Their councils must have authority of their own, or they won't trust us.
line.landler-question.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-question.text: The columns still need a route. Keep them on the railway where we can supply and control them, or send them through parallel valleys so one roadblock can't hold everyone? Commissar?
line.landler-question.choice.railway-axi: Drive the main force along the railway and seize each junction before the enemy can demolish it.
Gain a transport column, a larger prestige award and near-full core resupply, but forgo the parallel advance's core-wide experience.
line.landler-question.choice.parallel-co: Advance in parallel columns through the valleys so one roadblock cannot halt the whole operation.
Gain a prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the transport column and near-full resupply.
line.stromfeld-railway.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.stromfeld-railway.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.stromfeld-railway.text: The railway gives speed and supply, but it also makes our intention obvious. Keep flank detachments on the heights and engineers at the head of the column.
line.landler-columns.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-columns.text: Give the columns meeting points and keep them within supporting distance. If one is stopped, the others need to know before they move beyond it.
line.janousek-final.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.janousek-final.text: I'll send organisers behind the columns. Have the commanders enforce receipts for requisitions and leave elected councils in the villages. I can't persuade people to trust us if the next battalion ignores their decisions.
